newsitem.title: UK: Turkey Eurobond spreads seen widening.
newsitem.headline: Turkey Eurobond spreads seen widening.

text.p: Turkey's Eurobond spreads will likely widen gently after its foreign currency debt rating was cut on Thursday by Moody's Investors Service, dealers said.
"I can see spreads widening by five to 10 basis points," said a bond trader at a German bank in Frankfurt.
"The main action will happen tomorrow (Friday) morning. The announcement was too late (in European trading) to have a big impact today," he said.
Turkey's 7.75 percent mark Eurobond due 2004, launched in January, was marked down to 100.50/101.00 from 100.70/101.20 before the Moody's report. It ended Wednesday at 101.09.
A dealer at another German bank said while the market would take some comfort from the rating move having taken place, the outlook was, nevertheless, to the downside in the near term.

Moody's downgraded to B1 from Ba3 the long-term foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds of issuers domiciled in Turkey. Consequently, ratings on Turkey's foreign currency denominated bonds were lowered to B1.
Moody's said in early January it might downgrade Turkey.

Apart from its 500 million mark bond seven-year Eurobond in January via Commerzbank and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Turkey has also launched this year a 300 billion lire bond in February via Chase and Banca Commerciale Italiana.
Emerging market debt in general has come under pressure recently, hit by the uncertainty over U.S. interest rates.

Moody's said its action was prompted by Turkey's weak fiscal position, as well as concerns that political uncertainities might make it more difficult for the authorities to carry out essential reforms.
The public sector borrowing requirement was nearly 10 percent of GDP in 1996, and the budgetary stance remains essentially unchanged this year.
Moody's noted that privatization revenues were likely to increase from a very low base, but that official projections of $10 billion were unrealistic.
